evidenceRule: Capability claims are UNVERIFIED unless the tool was run. Metadata (stars, licence, version, last push) is VERIFIED (metadata). Vendor text is VERIFIED (vendor text), meaning the vendor said it.

tools.name: AIR Blackbox
tools.category: agent audit + EU AI Act scanner + runtime gate
tools.claimedArticles: Articles 9-15 (README); 51 checks across Articles 9-12, 14-15 (org repo description); 6 articles / 20+ checks (scanner repo)
tools.local: vendor states code is not sent anywhere
quotes: The flight recorder for autonomous AI agents. Record, replay, enforce, audit.
`air-blackbox comply` reads a codebase and reports gaps against the EU AI Act (Articles 9-15), GDPR and US state AI laws.
It runs locally, sends code nowhere, and is Apache 2.0.
We ran AIR and three other open-source EU AI Act scanners [...] on the same 144 hand-labelled programs, in six languages and forms.
notes: The 144-program benchmark is vendor-run and was not reproduced. It is not independent evidence.
Three AIR Blackbox surfaces state different coverage counts; a buyer should ask which number appears in the report.
The CLI is a hybrid of regex checks and a local fine-tuned model, not the MCP server alone.

correctionsToPriorMatrix.priorClaim: No verifiable AI-agent compliance product by that name was found; do not cite it as a competitor.
correctionsToPriorMatrix.correction: shadowaudit 0.6.3 is on PyPI and is deprecated in favour of capfence 0.9.0. It is a runtime authorization gateway, not a static scanner. It should be cited, but in the runtime column.
The main deliverable is the air-blackbox CLI (PyPI 1.17.0), with `air-blackbox comply` as the static scan command. The MCP repo is one surface among several.
